You are researching the local marketing ecosystem for a new dining-district brand in Danville, California ("Danville Dining District" / "South of Hartz" / #danvilleafterdark). The district is four restaurants at the corner of Hartz Ave and Church St at the south end of downtown: Rancho Cantina, Incontro Ristorante, Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar, and Danville Harvest. The partners want late-night (8-10pm) traffic, industry nights, cross-visits (dinner at one, nightcap and dessert at another), and later to invite the chamber of commerce, other Danville businesses and local influencers to join.
Tools: use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them with ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" first). You may also use Bash with curl (e.g. curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" URL | head -c 200000) to read pages that WebFetch cannot, and curl -sI to check headers. Do NOT use any browser tools (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__claude-in-chrome__*); the browser tab is reserved. Never guess: every fact must come from a page you actually read. If something cannot be found, leave it empty and say so in notes. Do not invent hours, prices, or dishes.
Find: (1) The Danville Area Chamber of Commerce (name, URL, contact, membership/marketing programs, restaurant-week or shop-local programs). (2) Other town organizations: Discover Danville / Town of Danville economic development, downtown business association, Danville Parks and Recreation events. (3) Recurring downtown events that draw evening crowds (Hot Summer Nights car show, Danville Farmers' Market, Lighting of the Old Oak Tree, Fourth of July parade, art walks, Devil Mountain Run, Danville Fall Crafts Festival) with dates and URLs. (4) Local food media and influencers: Diablo Magazine, DanvilleSanRamon.com, Patch, East Bay and Tri-Valley foodie Instagram accounts (handles and follower counts if visible), local podcasts. (5) Hashtags currently used for Danville dining and nightlife. (6) Existing restaurant week, dine-around or passport programs in Danville, San Ramon or the Tri-Valley the district could plug into. (7) The busier, younger nightlife cluster of restaurants and bars in Danville (where, which venues) so the site can position South of Hartz as the upscale alternative. Cite sources. Return only the structured object.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about Downtown Danville, California:

The town of Danville, east of San Francisco, has an enticing, vibrant downtown that's bursting with creative restaurants, with Hartz Avenue as the focal point. Downtown Danville's Hartz Avenue corridor is one of the most enjoyable dining stretches in the Tri-Valley.

**Restaurants & Dining:**
Some of the best restaurants in the downtown area include Bridges Restaurant and Bar (combining California cuisine with pan-Asian influences), Incontro Ristorante (serving Italian cuisine in the historic Hartz House), Crush'd Wine Bar Kitchen (featuring 24 wines on tap), and Taverna Sorrentina (serving Amalfi Coast-inspired Italian cooking). Sideboard Neighborhood Kitchen offers farm-to-table comfort food, fresh pastries, and artisan coffee.

**Shops:**
Downtown you'll find home decor, gourmet gifts, and local art in independently owned and expertly curated shops, offering something distinct from big-box retail.

**Events:**
Over 150 arts, crafts and food vendors line Hartz Avenue during the annual Danville Summerfest, where visitors can shop for handmade crafts and wonderful art or discover a treasure in one of the local shops.

The search results didn't return specific information about a "Discover Danville" app or the danville.com website itself, but they confirm the downtown area's reputation as a premier destination for shopping, dining, and community events.

# Danville Small Business Saturday & Main Street Designation Summary

**Main Street Designation:**
Danville has been officially designated as both a California Main Street and Main Street America affiliate community. According to Mayor Renee Morgan, this recognition honors "the Town's investment in our local businesses" and "the dedication of our business owners to our community."

**Date & Event:**
Small Business Saturday is scheduled for November 29, 2025. The Town will host live holiday music at Prospect Park Plaza from 1-3 p.m., with downtown shops offering special deals and free public parking.

**Programs & Initiatives:**

- **Discover Danville**: A free interactive mobile app enabling visitors to locate local businesses, find Small Business Saturday specials, vote for decorated storefronts, and track the Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt locations
- **Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt**: A children's activity running through January 4, where kids search for Auggie in participating downtown businesses

**Organizations Mentioned:**
No chamber of commerce or other business organizations are specifically named in this announcement. The focus centers on Town-sponsored initiatives and downtown retailers.

**Named Contact:**
Mayor Renee Morgan provided the official statement about the designation's significance.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the "Discover Danville" app:

## Overview
The Discover Danville walking tour app is now available to help visitors explore Danville with a web-based interactive tool that provides a unique way to incorporate hidden gems into a walking tour, including historic landmarks, local shops and restaurants.

## Accessing the App
Simply visit www.danville.ca.gov/DiscoverDanville on a mobile device to access the free, web-based app; no downloads or logins required.

## Features
The app features historical context, allowing users to view photos of "what used to be" while walking through Downtown Danville. Additionally, the Discover Danville app makes planning easier by highlighting nearby dog-friendly restaurants and shops as you explore, with an option to select "Dog Friendly" in the web-based app to navigate your pup through Downtown.

## Purpose
By guiding users through local retail and dining spots, Discover Danville promotes increased foot traffic to small businesses, supporting local entrepreneurs and helping sustain the Town's unique charm.

## Village Theatre Art Gallery

Located in the heart of downtown Danville, the Village Theatre offers a newly renovated Art Gallery. Built in 1873 for use as a farmer's lodge, the Village Theatre has been used as a Grange Hall, movie theatre, and church, and is recognized as a historic site by the Heritage Resource Commission.

The Village Theatre was renovated in 2009 with the lobby expanded to include an art gallery, which opened on November 14, 2009 and hosts quality art exhibits and receptions. The Art Gallery's Monday & Tuesday hours are by appointment only (call 925-314-3460 for appointments), and the theatre is open 1 hour before shows only.

The gallery regularly features exhibitions, such as "More Than a Line" which opened with a reception on Friday, July 10, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.

## Museum of the San Ramon Valley

The Museum is housed in the restored 1891 Southern Pacific Depot in Danville on Railroad Avenue at Prospect. The Museum of San Ramon Valley commemorates Danville's history as a railway depot and features a life-size train car that visitors are welcome to board and pose with. Founded in 1985, the Museum of the San Ramon Valley is dedicated to preserving and celebrating the region's rich history and heritage through exhibits, tours, archival collections, and special programs.

## Evening Events

The Town hosts "At the Plaza," a free entertainment series at Prospect Park Plaza, bringing the community together for family-friendly events, with live entertainment and special activities throughout the season, free to attend and no registration required.

# Danville's Proposed Permanent Outdoor Dining Rules

**Byline:** Jeremy Walsh | **Date:** September 7, 2026

## Rules Under Consideration

The Danville Planning Commission will discuss formalizing permanent regulations for outdoor dining on both public parking spots (parklets) and private property. Current temporary rules expire January 2, 2027.

## Key Provisions

**Public parklets:** Design standards, lease agreements, and a maximum of 12 downtown parking spots available for new parklet installations. After that limit, a waitlist would be created. Hartz Avenue is explicitly prohibited from parklet use.

**Private property seating:** Restaurants needing Design Review Board approval for new structures or facade alterations. The town would establish standards for in-lieu parking fees when applicable.

**Alcohol:** Parklets in public rights-of-way would require town exemptions to permit drinking in areas otherwise prohibited from alcohol consumption.

## Timing & Next Steps

The Planning Commission meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, September 8, 2026, at 5 p.m. at Town Meeting Hall, 201 Front Street. The proposal aims to transition from temporary to indefinite authorization of outdoor dining programs.

## Danville Loves Summer 2026

The Town of Danville launched Danville Loves Summer, a summer campaign highlighting the many ways to enjoy the community close to home, designed to help residents and visitors discover what is happening in Town and make the most of the season.

The Town invites the community to celebrate summer with At the Plaza, a free entertainment series at Prospect Park Plaza in the heart of Downtown Danville featuring live music and family-friendly activities throughout the season.

### Summer Entertainment

The Town offers free weekly entertainment through two favorite summer series: Music in the Park and Moonlight Movies, with community members invited to gather friends and family, bring a picnic, and enjoy an evening outside.

## Danville Hotel History

The Danville Hotel, a two-story, ten-room folk Victorian, was built after the Southern Pacific Railroad arrived in 1891. It was owned and operated by Edward and Mary McCauley and later by daughters Mollie and Nellie, providing bed, board and Mary's famous pies. When the hotel was moved to face Hartz Avenue in 1927, the veranda was added.

Beginning in 1932, renowned San Francisco Chef Paul Zeibig provided elegant, award-winning meals in the hotel which drew patrons from afar. In 1952 the lively Russel Glenn leased the hotel, buying it in 1956. He worked to make the hotel a tourist attraction, painting it red and white and adding a Ghost Town patio and other buildings.

## Modern Development

The site's two new buildings, each two-stories, will contain retail shops and restaurants on the ground floor with residential units above—16 luxury condos ranging in square footage from 919–1,432. Blossom & Root opened at Danville Hotel Town Center, and Berkeley-based olive oil and balsamic vinegar company Amphora opened recently at Danville Hotel Town Center where Papyrus used to be.

The Danville Hotel Town Center has become an important retail, restaurant, and residential district in Old Town Danville, featuring a mix of dining, shopping, and luxury residential spaces.

# Town of Danville Social Media Summary

**Date:** May 12, 2023

**Consolidated Accounts & Platforms:**
The Town unified its social media presence under the handle @DanvilleCAgov across Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. Previously separate accounts for Live Locally, Danville Parks, Village Theatre, and Art Gallery now feed into this single account. The Town also maintains a Nextdoor presence.

**Promoted Handle:**
@DanvilleCAgov is the primary social media identifier, mirroring the Town's website at www.danville.ca.gov.

**Additional Resources:**
- Danville Police Department maintains separate Facebook and newly launched Instagram accounts for safety alerts
- Residents can subscribe to Nixle for text-based emergency notifications
- www.danville.ca.gov/stayconnected provides social media links

**Community Participation:**
Residents are encouraged to follow @DanvilleCAgov for municipal updates including events, business openings, and construction projects. According to Public Information Officer Jenn Starnes, "you now only have to follow one account on your favorite platform for the latest news."

# Visit Tri-Valley Overview

## What It Is
Visit Tri-Valley is a destination marketing organization that promotes the Tri-Valley region as a tourism destination. As a 501(c)(6) nonprofit established in 2005, it "market[s] certain regions as desirable tourism destinations."

## Service Area & Funding
The organization represents four California communities: Danville, Dublin, Livermore, and Pleasanton. It operates through a bed tax model where "the visitor actually pays for Visit Tri-Valley through a nominal bed tax charged per room, per night."

## Marketing Programs for Businesses
Visit Tri-Valley offers several partnership opportunities:
- **Wine & Dine**: Highlights restaurants featuring local Livermore Valley wines with waived corkage fees
- **You Sip, We Ship**: Hotels participating in a wine shipping reimbursement program
- **Trail Passports**: Beer, caffeine, and ice cream trails that promote multiple businesses
- Business listing requests and partnership opportunities through their Business Hub

## Contact & Location
The organization maintains an online presence with social media accounts and offers a newsletter signup. Their website is visittrivalley.com, though a specific street address isn't provided on this page.

## Becoming a Partner
The page references a "Tri-Valley Business Listing Request" link, suggesting interested Danville restaurants should submit through their formal business partnership process via their website.

chamber.name: Danville Area Chamber of Commerce
chamber.contact: 117-E Town and Country Drive, Danville, CA 94526 | (925) 837-4400 | office@danvilleareachamber.com (general) | events@danvilleareachamber.com (events/sponsorships). Staff (per chamber staff page): Amy Millington, President (president@danvilleareachamber.com); Noemi Chojnacka, Member Services Manager | Office (x1801); Karen Stevenot, Events Manager (x1804). Note: the Tri-Valley Chamber Alliance page still lists Judy Lloyd as President/CEO, so that page appears out of date. Social: Instagram @danvilleareachamber, Facebook /DanvilleAreaChamber, LinkedIn. Member portal + public event calendar: https://business.danvilleareachamber.com/
chamber.programs: Founded New Year's Eve 1948; serves Danville, Alamo, Blackhawk and Diablo. Roughly 500-600 member businesses, 4 staff, 15-member board (per Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance). Member benefits (per Why Join page): online business directory listing, Member-to-Member Deals, newsletter features, social media promotion, ribbon cuttings, monthly mixers, referral/leads groups (Sunrise Alliance, Diablo Business Network), free small-business workshops, private meeting room access, grant navigation, signature-event access. MOST RELEVANT PROGRAMS FOR THE DISTRICT: (1) Sip & Stroll - the chamber's 20-year signature wine-stroll, Thursday May 7 2026, 5:30-8:30pm, ~35 participating businesses across downtown Danville AND the Danville Livery, $65 tasting / $20 designated driver, includes commemorative wine glass, tote, live music and FREE TROLLEY between downtown and the Livery. Businesses join by submitting the 'Become a Participating Business' form to events@danvilleareachamber.com and choosing a sponsorship level. (2) Fall Hallo-Wine - Oct 28 2026, downtown (chamber-run fall counterpart to Sip & Stroll; earlier years ran as Flavors of Fall, Oktoberfest and Fall Rock & Stroll). (3) Lighting of the Old Oak Tree - Nov 27 2026, downtown (49th edition was Nov 28 2025, program 5pm, tree lit ~6:30pm, on Diablo Rd between W El Pintado and I-680; run with the Town). (4) Paws & Claws in Downtown Danville - Dec 10 2026. (5) Passport to Wellness - June 13 2026. (6) Other: State of the Town, Community Awards Celebration/Gala, Women's Enterprise Initiative, historically two annual arts & crafts fairs (Summerfest in June and Fallfest in October). The chamber does NOT run a restaurant week; its dining-adjacent vehicle is the seasonal wine/beer stroll series. Member of the Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance (trivalleychambers.org) alongside Dublin, Livermore Valley, Pleasanton and San Ramon chambers.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - Economic Development Division
town_orgs.note: Primary town contact. Melysa Vander Mel, Supervisor of Economic Development (also listed elsewhere as Economic Development Specialist), 925-314-3379, mvandermel@danville.ca.gov. Offers: Business Concierge (guides businesses through development review), Business Boost Grant Program, Business Funding Support described as grants to market businesses OR to fund collaborative community events (directly relevant - a four-restaurant district event is exactly the collaborative-event framing), market analysis/demographics, business library, sign permits, TEMPORARY OUTDOOR PERMITS, and downtown employee parking permits.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - 'Live Locally' branding & marketing campaign
town_orgs.note: The Town's official place brand, tagline 'Live Locally' / 'So much to do...so little time.' Includes custom logos, color palette and photography, and the official hashtag #LiveLocallyDanville, which residents, business owners and visitors are explicitly asked to use. Rolled out across all Town digital and print channels. Contact for business use: Melysa Vander Mel.

town_orgs.name: Discover Danville (Town of Danville web app)
town_orgs.note: Free web-based walking-tour app - no download or login. Maps historic landmarks, local shops and restaurants, shows historical 'what used to be' photos, and has a dog-friendly filter. Explicitly built to drive foot traffic to small businesses. Also used as the delivery channel for Small Business Saturday specials, decorated-storefront voting and the Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt. A district listing/route here is a free, high-leverage ask.

town_orgs.name: California Main Street / Main Street America designation
town_orgs.note: Danville was officially designated both a California Main Street and Main Street America affiliate community (announced alongside Small Business Saturday, Nov 29 2025). Mayor Renee Morgan framed it as recognition of the Town's investment in local business. Useful hook for positioning a new dining district as part of the Main Street story.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - Recreation, Arts & Community Services (RACS)
town_orgs.note: 925-314-3400, recreation@danville.ca.gov. Runs the Town's free entertainment programming: Music at the Plaza and 'At the Plaza' series at Prospect Park Plaza (downtown), Music in the Park, Moonlight Movies, Kidchella, Art in the Park, Howl-o-Ween, Spooktacular. Also operates the Village Theatre & Art Gallery, 233 Front Street (925-314-3460), which produces evening shows - e.g. 'Mortified' at 8pm - and gallery opening receptions (5:30-7:30pm), both of which release a downtown audience right into the 8-10pm window the district wants.

town_orgs.name: Visit Tri-Valley (regional destination marketing organization)
town_orgs.note: 501(c)(6) established 2005, funded by a per-room bed tax, in partnership with the cities/chambers of Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin and the Town of Danville. Programs a district can join: Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week, Wine & Dine (restaurants featuring Livermore Valley wines with waived corkage), You Sip We Ship, and Trail Passports (beer, caffeine and ice cream trails). Business listing requests via their Business Hub; sponsorship contact info@visittrivalley.

town_orgs.name: Danville Merchants' Association
town_orgs.note: Named by the Town as the organizer of the Hot Summer Sundays Car Show. No standalone website, social account or contact page found - may operate informally through the car-show organizers. Worth a direct ask via the Town's Economic Development office.

town_orgs.name: Discover Danville Association Inc.
town_orgs.note: CAUTION - appears defunct. A 501(c)(6) business league (EIN 20-2846642) of downtown Danville businesses formed to improve economic vibrancy, town centricity and tourism 'while maintaining the village atmosphere.' Last IRS filing was FY2016 (revenue -$773, net assets $0) and it is not in the IRS's most recent list of tax-exempt organizations. It historically received Town business-promotion funds. Do not build outreach plans around it without confirming it still exists. Note also that 'Discover Danville' now primarily refers to the Town's walking-tour app, and that discoverdanvilleca.com is an unrelated spam travel blog.

town_orgs.name: Museum of the San Ramon Valley
town_orgs.note: 205 Railroad Avenue (the restored 1891 Southern Pacific Depot), 925-837-3750, info@museumsrv.org. Runs Shops & Hops (the Danville craft beer stroll) and the Summer Soiree. Has a formal sponsorship program at museumsrv.org/sponsorship/. Its events are the closest existing analogue to a walkable multi-venue evening in Danville.

town_orgs.name: Danville Lions Club
town_orgs.note: Organizes 'A Taste of Danville' - the 29th annual Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk. This is the single most direct existing dine-around the district should join. Proceeds benefit Lions Club Charities, the Lions Blind Center and educational scholarships.

town_orgs.name: Kiwanis Club of San Ramon Valley

town_orgs.name: Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance (TVCCA)

town_orgs.name: Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association (PCFMA)

The most reliable weekly downtown footfall - a daytime sampling table here converts well into evening reservations.

events.name: A Taste of Danville - 29th Annual Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk
events.note: Prospect Park Plaza, 396 Hartz Ave. $45 food tasting ticket, $25 beer-and-wine pavilion; live music and dancing. Supported by the Town as part of a Council-approved program. dine_programs.name: Visit Tri-Valley Trail Passports (beer, caffeine and ice cream trails)

dine_programs.name: Visit Tri-Valley 'Wine & Dine'

dine_programs.name: Discover Danville walking-tour web app (Town of Danville)

Nonprofit local news for the Tri-Valley covering Danville, Alamo, Blackhawk and Diablo; part of the Embarcadero Media Foundation family (with Pleasanton Weekly, Livermore Vine, Palo Alto Online and others). Reporter/editor Jeremy Walsh already covers this exact beat - he wrote the May 4, 2026 piece on Rancho Cantina's Danville opening (naming 501 Hartz Ave, the southeast corner of Hartz and Church, in the former Cocina Hermanas space, and referencing Danville Harvest at 500 Hartz) and the Sept 7, 2026 piece on the Planning Commission's permanent outdoor-dining rules. Contacts: editor@DanvilleSanRamon.com, letters@DanvilleSanRamon.com, ads@DanvilleSanRamon.com. No public staff directory - go through the editorial address or the contact form.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Deborah Grossman - 'Tri-Valley Foodist' columnist
local_media_and_influencers.note: Writes about local restaurants, wineries, breweries and distilleries for Embarcadero Media East Bay (runs on both DanvilleSanRamon.com and PleasantonWeekly.com). Direct email listed: deborah@deborahgrossman.com. She has already written on the Danville brewery scene (May 26, 2025) and covers Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week every year. The single most targetable food byline in the market.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Diablo Magazine
local_media_and_influencers.note: The East Bay's glossy of record. Runs a Food News section, the 'Diablo Dish' openings blog (which covered Canyon Club Brewery's Danville expansion), and the annual reader-voted Best of the East Bay awards at vote.diablomag.com. Its Best of results get syndicated into Patch coverage for every Tri-Valley town. Also published the East Bay social-media-influencer roundup used below.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Patch
local_media_and_influencers.note: Hyperlocal aggregator with dedicated Restaurants & Bars and Business sections. Reliably re-reports openings, closings and awards - it has covered Taverna Sorrentina's opening, Canyon Club's Danville expansion and the Best of the East Bay lists. Michael Wittner is a Patch staff byline on Danville business coverage. Low-effort, high-frequency placement.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Social (Heather Ruiz)
local_media_and_influencers.note: HIGHEST-VALUE LOCAL INFLUENCER. Founded ~2018 by Heather Ruiz; roughly 11K Instagram followers and 10K+ website views/month. Tagline 'Be Seen. Support Local.' Covers restaurants, happy hours, events, holiday activities and business spotlights, and maintains a Danville business directory. Already publishes a Danville happy-hour guide that lists Danville Harvest (500 Hartz Ave, happy hour 7 days/week 3:30-5pm). Openly sells advertising: website placements, social media packages and featured write-ups. Phone (619) 944-5360. Note her happy-hour guide still lists the now-closed Cocina Hermanas, so an update pitch is a natural opening.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Your Town Monthly
local_media_and_influencers.note: Local lifestyle publication from S and J Advertising covering 12 East Bay and Solano communities including Danville, Pleasanton, Walnut Creek, Dublin and Livermore. Runs a recurring 'Taste of Your Town' restaurant spotlight - it profiled Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar (480 Hartz Ave) in August 2026, written by Assul Coss. Also runs an events calendar that carries Danville events (Hot Summer Sundays, Sip & Stroll, A Taste of Danville). Two of the four district restaurants are already in their orbit.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Beyond the Creek
local_media_and_influencers.note: Local news and lifestyle blog covering the greater Danville/Walnut Creek area with sections for restaurants, shopping, real estate and neighborhoods. Broke the Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar opening and covers the Danville Hotel Town Center tenant churn. Runs a newsletter and an advertiser program. Fast, informal - good for openings and 'new late menu' news.

local_media_and_influencers.name: ALIVE East Bay Magazine
local_media_and_influencers.note: ALIVE Media, 3200A Danville Blvd., Suite 204, Alamo, CA 94507 - physically in the district's own backyard. Regional lifestyle glossy.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Living
local_media_and_influencers.note: Best Version Media community magazine launched March 2016, mailed to Danville residents, built around neighbor-submitted stories and 'local, trusted businesses.' Also on Issuu. Pure resident-reach play rather than a food outlet.

The Town consolidated its Live Locally, Parks, Village Theatre and Art Gallery accounts into this single handle in May 2023; Public Information Officer Jenn Starnes. local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Farmers' Market

local_media_and_influencers.note: 466,000 Instagram followers per Diablo Magazine (July 2022). A DANVILLE RESIDENT and best-selling gluten-free cookbook author. The highest-reach influencer who actually lives in town - a gluten-free-friendly late menu or a private tasting is an obvious hook.

competitor_nightlife_zone.where: The NORTH end of downtown Danville - the 100-400 blocks of Hartz Avenue plus the Railroad Avenue / Prospect Avenue corridor, anchored by the Danville Hotel Town Center on Railroad Ave. That is roughly five to six blocks north of the district. For contrast, the four South of Hartz venues sit tightly clustered at the Hartz-and-Church corner: Incontro Ristorante 455 Hartz Ave (the historic Hartz House), Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar 480 Hartz Ave, Danville Harvest 500 Hartz Ave, and Rancho Cantina 501 Hartz Ave (the southeast corner of Hartz and Church, in the former Cocina Hermanas space). A secondary, separate late cluster sits southeast of downtown at the Danville Livery shopping center, 204 Sycamore Valley Road W, where Canyon Club Brewery runs a biergarten with firepits, heat lamps and a live-music stage.
example_venues: Elliott's Bar - 369 Hartz Ave. A dive bar in business over 100 years (briefly an ice cream parlor during Prohibition). Open 10:00 a.m. to 1:30 a.m. daily - by a wide margin the latest-closing venue in downtown Danville and the default destination after every other kitchen shuts.
Auburn Lounge & Wine Bar - 321 Hartz Ave. 1930s speakeasy feel. Mon-Wed 4 p.m.-midnight, Thu-Sun 2 p.m.-midnight.

Revel Kitchen & Bar - 331 Hartz Ave. Upscale-casual tavern from the owners of Esin, craft beer, cocktails and an eclectic wine list. Notably closes 9:00 p.m. Sun-Thu and 9:30 p.m. Fri-Sat, which is exactly the gap the district is targeting.
Danville Brewing Co. / DBC - 200 Railroad Ave, in the Danville Hotel Town Center. House beers plus guest drafts; a 2026 Diablo Magazine Best of the East Bay winner (Burger).

Crush'd Wine Bar Kitchen - downtown Danville. 24 wines on tap, craft cocktails, Apertivo Hour 3-6 p.m. daily ($12 cocktails, $9 small bites) and Live Music Thursdays. Markets itself explicitly 'from brunch to late night' - the closest direct competitor to the district's positioning.
11th Tiger - 171 Hartz Ave
Locanda Ravello - 172 E Prospect Ave
Le Petit Corner - 345 Railroad Ave
Primo's Pizzeria & Pub - downtown; happy hour daily 3-6 p.m.
The Growler - happy hour Tuesdays 4-9 p.m., Wed-Fri 3-6 p.m.

Canyon Club Brewery - Danville Livery, 204 Sycamore Valley Rd W (separate cluster southeast of downtown). Taproom, restaurant and pilot brewery with a patio biergarten, firepits and a live-music stage.
competitor_nightlife_zone.description: Danville's noisier, younger, later-running drinking scene is concentrated at the top of Hartz Avenue and around the Danville Hotel Town Center on Railroad Ave, not at the Church Street end. The mix there is a century-old dive (Elliott's, open to 1:30 a.m.), a speakeasy-styled wine lounge (Auburn), a brewery taproom (Danville Brewing) and a self-described 'brunch to late night' wine bar (Crush'd) - venues built around drinking, standing and staying, with a beer-and-cocktail price point. The Danville Livery biergarten pulls a similar crowd off-downtown. Three things make South of Hartz's upscale-alternative positioning defensible. First, geography: the four district restaurants form a genuinely contiguous four-corner block at Hartz and Church, five-plus blocks from that cluster - close enough to be downtown, far enough to read as its own place. Second, the 8-10 p.m. gap is real and documented, not assumed: even the good sit-down rooms at the north end close at 9-9:30 p.m., and a Tri-Valley Foodist piece quoted a local observing that restaurants in Danville get all the attention, i.e. the town is restaurant-centric rather than bar-centric. Third, the district's own mix is already differentiated - a historic-house Italian room, a tiki bar, a farm-to-table kitchen and a wood-fired Mexican cantina - which supports a dinner-here, nightcap-and-dessert-there cross-visit story that a row of bars cannot tell. The realistic competitive risk is Crush'd, which already claims the late-night language, and Elliott's, which owns the after-9:30 default by simple fact of being open.

input.notes: WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM (do not treat these as established): (1) FOLLOWER COUNTS. Instagram blocks automated reads, so every follower number here comes from a search-result snippet or a cited article, not from the profile itself. The @bayarea.foodies (255K IG / 334.1K TikTok) and @daniellewalker (466K) figures come from a Diablo Magazine roundup published July 15, 2022 and are certainly stale. @danvillesocial ~11K, @danvillecagov ~15K, @danvilleharvest ~2,750 and @eastbayeats ~4,518 come from search snippets quoting the live profiles. Re-verify manually before building a media plan around any of them. (2) DANVILLE FALLFEST STATUS. Fallfest is absent from the Town's 2026 community events list and danvillefallfest.com returned no content. It may be discontinued or folded into Fall Hallo-Wine. Its historic street closures included Church Street between Railroad and Hartz - the district's own corner - so its status matters. Confirm with the chamber. (3) FALL HALLO-WINE DETAILS. I have only the Town's one-line listing (Oct 28, 2026, chamber, downtown). No dedicated event page exists yet; earlier editions ran as Flavors of Fall, Oktoberfest and Fall Rock & Stroll. (4) 2027 TASTE TRI-VALLEY DATES are unannounced; the page says to watch it. (5) CHAMBER MEMBERSHIP PRICING is not published anywhere public - the Why Join page references a Membership Toolkit but shows no tiers or dollar figures. Ask Amy Millington directly. (6) NO LOCAL PODCAST FOUND. There is no Danville CA or Tri-Valley food/nightlife podcast that I could verify. The 'Danville Podcast' on Apple Podcasts is a high-school class production from a different Danville. Treat a podcast as a gap to create rather than a channel to pitch. (7) DISCOVER DANVILLE ASSOCIATION appears defunct (last IRS filing FY2016, absent from the current IRS exempt list). 'Discover Danville' today means the Town's walking-tour web app. Also note discoverdanvilleca.com is an unrelated spam travel blog and discoverdanville.com is Danville VIRGINIA - a large share of web results for 'Danville' are Virginia, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Illinois or Indiana, so verify the state on anything not sourced here. (8) DANVILLE MERCHANTS' ASSOCIATION has no findable website or contact; it is known only from the Town's attribution of the Hot Summer Sundays Car Show. (9) HASHTAG DATA comes from best-hashtags.com co-occurrence data (a real aggregation of Instagram usage), not from Instagram directly; treat relative popularity as indicative rather than exact. (10) HOURS quoted for competitor venues come from Yelp/OpenTable listings surfaced in search and change frequently - verify before publishing any comparison. THREE FINDINGS WORTH ACTING ON FIRST: (a) The brand names are CLEAN. best-hashtags.com returns 'not found' for #danvilleafterdark, #southofhartz AND #danvillenightlife - none of the three is currently in use, so the district can own all of them outright. (b) Danville Harvest is already credited by the Town as the organizer of a downtown Neighborhood Street Party (June 20, 2026), which means one of the four partners has already walked the Town's approval path for a street-level event. (c) The Town's Economic Development Division explicitly funds 'collaborative community events,' and none of the four restaurants won a 2026 Diablo Best of the East Bay award - so there is both money and an uncontested award category available. Also flag for the site build: the Planning Commission was reviewing PERMANENT outdoor-dining rules on Sept 8, 2026 (current temporary rules expire Jan 2, 2027), and the draft explicitly PROHIBITS parklets on Hartz Avenue while capping downtown parklets at 12 spaces - directly relevant to any patio-based late-night concept.

chamber.name: Danville Area Chamber of Commerce
chamber.contact: 117-E Town and Country Drive, Danville, CA 94526 | (925) 837-4400 | office@danvilleareachamber.com (general) | events@danvilleareachamber.com (events/sponsorships). Staff (per chamber staff page): Amy Millington, President (president@danvilleareachamber.com); Noemi Chojnacka, Member Services Manager | Office (x1801); Karen Stevenot, Events Manager (x1804). Note: the Tri-Valley Chamber Alliance page still lists Judy Lloyd as President/CEO, so that page appears out of date. Social: Instagram @danvilleareachamber, Facebook /DanvilleAreaChamber, LinkedIn. Member portal + public event calendar: https://business.danvilleareachamber.com/
chamber.programs: Founded New Year's Eve 1948; serves Danville, Alamo, Blackhawk and Diablo. Roughly 500-600 member businesses, 4 staff, 15-member board (per Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance). Member benefits (per Why Join page): online business directory listing, Member-to-Member Deals, newsletter features, social media promotion, ribbon cuttings, monthly mixers, referral/leads groups (Sunrise Alliance, Diablo Business Network), free small-business workshops, private meeting room access, grant navigation, signature-event access. MOST RELEVANT PROGRAMS FOR THE DISTRICT: (1) Sip & Stroll - the chamber's 20-year signature wine-stroll, Thursday May 7 2026, 5:30-8:30pm, ~35 participating businesses across downtown Danville AND the Danville Livery, $65 tasting / $20 designated driver, includes commemorative wine glass, tote, live music and FREE TROLLEY between downtown and the Livery. Businesses join by submitting the 'Become a Participating Business' form to events@danvilleareachamber.com and choosing a sponsorship level. (2) Fall Hallo-Wine - Oct 28 2026, downtown (chamber-run fall counterpart to Sip & Stroll; earlier years ran as Flavors of Fall, Oktoberfest and Fall Rock & Stroll). (3) Lighting of the Old Oak Tree - Nov 27 2026, downtown (49th edition was Nov 28 2025, program 5pm, tree lit ~6:30pm, on Diablo Rd between W El Pintado and I-680; run with the Town). (4) Paws & Claws in Downtown Danville - Dec 10 2026. (5) Passport to Wellness - June 13 2026. (6) Other: State of the Town, Community Awards Celebration/Gala, Women's Enterprise Initiative, historically two annual arts & crafts fairs (Summerfest in June and Fallfest in October). The chamber does NOT run a restaurant week; its dining-adjacent vehicle is the seasonal wine/beer stroll series. Member of the Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance (trivalleychambers.org) alongside Dublin, Livermore Valley, Pleasanton and San Ramon chambers.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - Economic Development Division
town_orgs.note: Primary town contact. Melysa Vander Mel, Supervisor of Economic Development (also listed elsewhere as Economic Development Specialist), 925-314-3379, mvandermel@danville.ca.gov. Offers: Business Concierge (guides businesses through development review), Business Boost Grant Program, Business Funding Support described as grants to market businesses OR to fund collaborative community events (directly relevant - a four-restaurant district event is exactly the collaborative-event framing), market analysis/demographics, business library, sign permits, TEMPORARY OUTDOOR PERMITS, and downtown employee parking permits.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - 'Live Locally' branding & marketing campaign
town_orgs.note: The Town's official place brand, tagline 'Live Locally' / 'So much to do...so little time.' Includes custom logos, color palette and photography, and the official hashtag #LiveLocallyDanville, which residents, business owners and visitors are explicitly asked to use. Rolled out across all Town digital and print channels. Contact for business use: Melysa Vander Mel.

town_orgs.name: Discover Danville (Town of Danville web app)
town_orgs.note: Free web-based walking-tour app - no download or login. Maps historic landmarks, local shops and restaurants, shows historical 'what used to be' photos, and has a dog-friendly filter. Explicitly built to drive foot traffic to small businesses. Also used as the delivery channel for Small Business Saturday specials, decorated-storefront voting and the Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt. A district listing/route here is a free, high-leverage ask.

town_orgs.name: California Main Street / Main Street America designation
town_orgs.note: Danville was officially designated both a California Main Street and Main Street America affiliate community (announced alongside Small Business Saturday, Nov 29 2025). Mayor Renee Morgan framed it as recognition of the Town's investment in local business. Useful hook for positioning a new dining district as part of the Main Street story.

town_orgs.name: Town of Danville - Recreation, Arts & Community Services (RACS)
town_orgs.note: 925-314-3400, recreation@danville.ca.gov. Runs the Town's free entertainment programming: Music at the Plaza and 'At the Plaza' series at Prospect Park Plaza (downtown), Music in the Park, Moonlight Movies, Kidchella, Art in the Park, Howl-o-Ween, Spooktacular. Also operates the Village Theatre & Art Gallery, 233 Front Street (925-314-3460), which produces evening shows - e.g. 'Mortified' at 8pm - and gallery opening receptions (5:30-7:30pm), both of which release a downtown audience right into the 8-10pm window the district wants.

town_orgs.name: Visit Tri-Valley (regional destination marketing organization)
town_orgs.note: 501(c)(6) established 2005, funded by a per-room bed tax, in partnership with the cities/chambers of Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin and the Town of Danville. Programs a district can join: Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week, Wine & Dine (restaurants featuring Livermore Valley wines with waived corkage), You Sip We Ship, and Trail Passports (beer, caffeine and ice cream trails). Business listing requests via their Business Hub; sponsorship contact info@visittrivalley.

town_orgs.name: Danville Merchants' Association
town_orgs.note: Named by the Town as the organizer of the Hot Summer Sundays Car Show. No standalone website, social account or contact page found - may operate informally through the car-show organizers. Worth a direct ask via the Town's Economic Development office.

town_orgs.name: Discover Danville Association Inc.
town_orgs.note: CAUTION - appears defunct. A 501(c)(6) business league (EIN 20-2846642) of downtown Danville businesses formed to improve economic vibrancy, town centricity and tourism 'while maintaining the village atmosphere.' Last IRS filing was FY2016 (revenue -$773, net assets $0) and it is not in the IRS's most recent list of tax-exempt organizations. It historically received Town business-promotion funds. Do not build outreach plans around it without confirming it still exists. Note also that 'Discover Danville' now primarily refers to the Town's walking-tour app, and that discoverdanvilleca.com is an unrelated spam travel blog.

town_orgs.name: Museum of the San Ramon Valley
town_orgs.note: 205 Railroad Avenue (the restored 1891 Southern Pacific Depot), 925-837-3750, info@museumsrv.org. Runs Shops & Hops (the Danville craft beer stroll) and the Summer Soiree. Has a formal sponsorship program at museumsrv.org/sponsorship/. Its events are the closest existing analogue to a walkable multi-venue evening in Danville.

town_orgs.name: Danville Lions Club
town_orgs.note: Organizes 'A Taste of Danville' - the 29th annual Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk. This is the single most direct existing dine-around the district should join. Proceeds benefit Lions Club Charities, the Lions Blind Center and educational scholarships.

town_orgs.name: Kiwanis Club of San Ramon Valley
town_orgs.note: Organizes the Kiwanis-Danville 4th of July Parade with the Town. parade@srvkiwanis.org, 925-272-8207. Sponsorship tiers Presenting / Diamond / Platinum / Gold / Silver / Bronze; free parade entry at $1,000+. Mandatory entrant meeting held the preceding June.

town_orgs.name: Danville d'Elegance Foundation
town_orgs.note: Organizes the Danville Concours d'Elegance car show on Hartz & Prospect Avenues each September.

town_orgs.name: Tri-Valley Chamber of Commerce Alliance (TVCCA)
town_orgs.note: Alliance of the Danville, Dublin, Livermore Valley, Pleasanton and San Ramon chambers - a route to reach industry/hospitality staff across the whole Tri-Valley for industry nights.

town_orgs.name: Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association (PCFMA)
town_orgs.note: The Town's approved operator of the Danville Farmers' Market for the last ~20 years. Market Instagram: @danvillecafm.

events.name: Danville Farmers' Market
events.when: Every Saturday, 9 a.m.-1 p.m., year-round, rain or shine
events.note: Railroad Avenue Municipal Parking Lot at the corner of Railroad and Prospect Avenues (205 Railroad Ave). Operated by PCFMA as the Town's approved operator. Instagram @danvillecafm. The most reliable weekly downtown footfall - a daytime sampling table here converts well into evening reservations.

events.name: A Taste of Danville - 29th Annual Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk
events.note: Prospect Park Plaza, 396 Hartz Ave. $45 food tasting ticket, $25 beer-and-wine pavilion; live music and dancing. Supported by the Town as part of a Council-approved program. Tickets via Eventbrite. THE most relevant existing event - a walkable multi-restaurant tasting on a weeknight in exactly the district's target hours. Contact the Danville Lions Club to be a tasting stop.

events.name: Sip & Stroll (Danville Area Chamber of Commerce)
events.note: ~35 participating businesses across downtown Danville and the Danville Livery. $65 tasting / $20 designated driver. Includes commemorative wine glass, tote bag, live music and a free trolley between downtown and the Livery. Chamber's signature event for 20+ years. Businesses apply via the 'Become a Participating Business' form emailed to events@danvilleareachamber.com.

events.name: Shops & Hops (Danville Craft Beer Stroll)
events.note: Organized by the Museum of the San Ramon Valley as a fundraiser. $35 tasting ticket, $10 designated driver. Format: participants stroll downtown shops and venues for craft beer tastings. A recent edition sold nearly all 320 tickets with 10 regional breweries pouring at 9 venues. Sponsors have included Danville Brewery, Canyon Club, Trumer Pils, Dust Bowl and The Growler.

events.name: Devil Mountain Run
events.note: Start/finish 345 Railroad Avenue, downtown Danville. USATF-certified 5K and 10K (new courses for 2026), Mile of Truth, Buddi Love Dog Mile and a free Kids Fun Run. Free tech shirts to the first 1,000 paid registrants. Organized by Team Blue Sky Events per the Town's community events list. Morning event - brunch/late-breakfast opportunity, not an 8-10pm play.

events.name: Kiwanis-Danville 4th of July Parade
events.note: Route runs Hartz Avenue and San Ramon Valley Blvd from San Ramon Valley High School at Railroad Avenue to Town & Country Drive - i.e. straight past the district. The Town warns downtown will be very crowded before, during AND after. Sponsorship tiers Presenting through Bronze; free parade entry at $1,000+. Mandatory entrants' meeting the preceding June. parade@srvkiwanis.org, 925-272-8207.

events.name: Hot Summer Sundays Car Show
events.note: Hundreds of hot rods, classics, customs and exotics line Hartz Avenue downtown, with live DJs, local vendors and food/cafe specials. Spectator admission FREE; vehicle registration $40 pre-reg / $50 day-of (cash only day-of), registration opens May 1. Vehicles stage at San Ramon Valley HS at 8 a.m. Listed by the Town as organized by the Danville Merchants' Association. Vendor and sponsor slots available - contact David, ezasugo@yahoo.com / 925-437-3649. Ends at 4pm, so the natural district play is capturing the crowd as the show breaks up.

events.name: Danville Concours d'Elegance Car Show
events.note: Historic Downtown Danville at Hartz & Prospect Avenues. Organized by the Danville d'Elegance Foundation; supported by the Town under a Council-approved program.

events.name: San Ramon Valley High School Homecoming Parade
events.note: Downtown Danville. Listed on the Town's community events calendar. Family/alumni crowd.

events.name: Music at the Plaza / 'At the Plaza' free entertainment series
events.when: 2026 downtown dates included June 6, June 20, July 18, Aug 8, Aug 22 and Sept 5; winter/spring editions Jan 17, Feb 14, Mar 14 (1-3 p.m.)
events.note: Prospect Park Plaza, in the heart of downtown. Free, no registration. Live music, arts and crafts, family activities. Run by Town Recreation, Arts & Community Services (925-314-3400, recreation@danville.ca.gov). Summer series opened Saturday May 23, 2026.

events.name: Music in the Park and Moonlight Movies
events.when: Summer 2026: Music in the Park June 13, June 27, July 11, July 25; Moonlight Movies June 19, July 3, July 17, July 31
events.note: Free Town summer series. Music in the Park is historically at Oak Hill Park (3005 Stone Valley Road) with occasional Town Green dates - NOT downtown, so lower value for walk-in capture than the Plaza series. Part of the Town's 'Danville Loves Summer' campaign and online guide at danville.ca.gov/summer, updated weekly.

events.name: Neighborhood Street Party (hosted by Danville Harvest)
events.note: IMPORTANT PRECEDENT: the Town's own community events list credits Danville Harvest - one of the four district restaurants - as the organizer of a downtown street party. There is already an approved pathway for a district restaurant to run its own street-level event.

events.name: Flannel & Foliage: An Autumn Weekend in Danville
events.note: New for 2026. A 'Gilmore Girls'-inspired autumn weekend produced by Small Town Venture: free General Admission plus limited paid VIP, cast photo ops, autographs and small-group Q&As. Venue and talent contracts were still being signed as of the announcement, and local business participation was not yet addressed - which means the district could still get in early. Group lodging block at Hyatt House San Ramon (code G-STVG). Follow @smalltownventure; email alerts at smalltownventure.kit.com. This one brings out-of-town, evening-oriented, younger visitors - the best single fit for #danvilleafterdark.

events.name: Fall Hallo-Wine (Danville Area Chamber of Commerce)
events.note: Downtown Danville. The chamber's autumn wine/beer stroll, successor to earlier editions run as Flavors of Fall (2022), Oktoberfest (2024) and Fall Rock & Stroll (2023). I could not find a dedicated 2026 event page - confirm details with events@danvilleareachamber.com.

events.name: Lighting of the Old Oak Tree
events.note: Danville Area Chamber of Commerce in partnership with the Town, rain or shine. Evening program starts 5 p.m. near the Old Oak Tree on Diablo Road between West El Pintado and the I-680 freeway; local choirs, a guest performer, the Mayor's holiday message, and Father Christmas and the Snow Angel leading the countdown to the lighting by 6:30 p.m. The single biggest after-dark downtown crowd of the year, and it ends right at dinner hour. Info: 925-837-4400.

events.name: Small Business Saturday in Danville
events.when: Saturday after Thanksgiving (2025 edition was Nov 29)
events.note: Live holiday music at Prospect Park Plaza 1-3 p.m., downtown shop specials and free public parking. Specials and the decorated-storefront vote are distributed through the Discover Danville app; the Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt runs in participating downtown businesses through early January.

events.name: Paws & Claws in Downtown Danville
events.note: Danville Area Chamber of Commerce, downtown. Danville is heavily marketed as dog-friendly (the Discover Danville app has a dog-friendly filter), so patio-forward district venues fit naturally.

events.name: Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week
events.when: February 20 - March 1, 2026 (10 days); 2027 dates not yet announced
events.note: See dine_programs - listed here because it is the region's anchor dining event and the district should be registered before the 2027 announcement.

events.name: Danville Fallfest ('faire of 1,000 pumpkins')
events.when: Historically a Saturday-Sunday in October, 10 a.m.-5 p.m. - STATUS UNCERTAIN FOR 2026
events.note: Danville Area Chamber event with 100+ street vendors, hand-blown pumpkins, live music, kids' costume parade, and a Sunday classic car show. Historically closed Hartz Avenue (Diablo Rd to Hartz Way), Prospect Avenue, CHURCH STREET (Railroad to Hartz) and School Street - i.e. it closed the district's own corner. It does NOT appear on the Town's 2026 community events list and danvillefallfest.com returned no content, so it may be discontinued or folded into Fall Hallo-Wine. Verify with the chamber before planning around it.

dine_programs.name: Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week (Visit Tri-Valley)
dine_programs.note: The region's anchor dine-around. 10 days spanning Danville, Dublin, Livermore and Pleasanton; 2026 ran Feb 20 - Mar 1 with a finale cocktail party Feb 27. PARTICIPATION IS FREE. Restaurants, wineries, breweries, bakeries and cafes register via a Google Form linked from the page. Mechanic: a free mobile passport where each check-in (purchase required) is one entry in a Grand Prize Giveaway of dining certificates, wine tastings and culinary experiences. 2027 dates not yet announced - the page says to watch that URL. Sponsorship contact info@visittrivalley. This is the highest-value, lowest-cost program for the district to join, and the passport mechanic is directly transferable to a South of Hartz cross-visit card.

dine_programs.name: A Taste of Danville - Danville Lions Club Restaurant Walk
dine_programs.note: 29th annual in 2026. Tuesday June 2, 2026, 6-8:30 p.m., staged from Prospect Park Plaza (396 Hartz Ave). $45 food tasting / $25 beer-and-wine pavilion, live music and dancing. Benefits Lions Club Charities, the Lions Blind Center and scholarships. Town-supported under a Council-approved program. Danville's own restaurant walk and the closest existing thing to a dine-around at the district's target hours - joining as a cluster of four adjacent stops would be a natural pitch.

dine_programs.name: Sip & Stroll (Danville Area Chamber of Commerce)
dine_programs.note: Retail-and-tasting stroll, ~35 businesses across downtown and the Danville Livery, with a free trolley connecting the two. $65 / $20 DD. Note it is retail-tasting led rather than restaurant led, which leaves a real opening for a restaurant-led equivalent.

dine_programs.name: Shops & Hops (Museum of the San Ramon Valley)
dine_programs.note: Annual craft beer stroll through downtown Danville shops and venues, $35/$10 DD. A recent edition put 10 regional breweries in 9 venues and nearly sold out its 320 tickets. Proves demand for a ticketed, walkable, multi-stop evening in this exact downtown.

dine_programs.name: Visit Tri-Valley Trail Passports (beer, caffeine and ice cream trails)
dine_programs.note: Standing year-round mobile passports that promote multiple businesses across the Tri-Valley. A dessert/nightcap stop could plausibly fit an existing trail, or the district could propose a new one - the DMO already owns the platform and the audience.

dine_programs.name: Visit Tri-Valley 'Wine & Dine'
dine_programs.note: Restaurants featuring Livermore Valley wines with waived corkage fees. Low-cost way for the district to appear in DMO channels and to build a local-wine angle into a late menu.

dine_programs.name: Discover Danville walking-tour web app (Town of Danville)
dine_programs.note: Free, Town-run, no download required. Maps historic landmarks, shops and restaurants with a dog-friendly filter, and is the delivery channel for Small Business Saturday specials and the Auggie the Elf Holiday Hunt. Getting the four venues added - ideally as a named route - is the cheapest official distribution available.

dine_programs.name: Diablo Magazine 'Best of the East Bay' readers' choice awards
dine_programs.note: Annual reader vote across restaurants, bars and more; winners run in the July issue and are then amplified by Patch in every Tri-Valley town. 26 Danville businesses won in 2026 - including Danville Brewing Co. (Burger), Blossom and Root (Vegan) and Forbes Mill Steakhouse (Steak House) - but NONE of the four district restaurants appeared. An open, winnable target, especially in an uncontested category like a cocktail/tiki or late-night category.

local_media_and_influencers.name: DanvilleSanRamon.com (Danville Express / Embarcadero Media Foundation)
local_media_and_influencers.note: TOP PRIORITY. Nonprofit local news for the Tri-Valley covering Danville, Alamo, Blackhawk and Diablo; part of the Embarcadero Media Foundation family (with Pleasanton Weekly, Livermore Vine, Palo Alto Online and others). Reporter/editor Jeremy Walsh already covers this exact beat - he wrote the May 4, 2026 piece on Rancho Cantina's Danville opening (naming 501 Hartz Ave, the southeast corner of Hartz and Church, in the former Cocina Hermanas space, and referencing Danville Harvest at 500 Hartz) and the Sept 7, 2026 piece on the Planning Commission's permanent outdoor-dining rules. Contacts: editor@DanvilleSanRamon.com, letters@DanvilleSanRamon.com, ads@DanvilleSanRamon.com. No public staff directory - go through the editorial address or the contact form.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Deborah Grossman - 'Tri-Valley Foodist' columnist
local_media_and_influencers.note: Writes about local restaurants, wineries, breweries and distilleries for Embarcadero Media East Bay (runs on both DanvilleSanRamon.com and PleasantonWeekly.com). Direct email listed: deborah@deborahgrossman.com. She has already written on the Danville brewery scene (May 26, 2025) and covers Taste Tri-Valley Restaurant Week every year. The single most targetable food byline in the market.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Diablo Magazine
local_media_and_influencers.note: The East Bay's glossy of record. Runs a Food News section, the 'Diablo Dish' openings blog (which covered Canyon Club Brewery's Danville expansion), and the annual reader-voted Best of the East Bay awards at vote.diablomag.com. Its Best of results get syndicated into Patch coverage for every Tri-Valley town. Also published the East Bay social-media-influencer roundup used below.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Patch
local_media_and_influencers.note: Hyperlocal aggregator with dedicated Restaurants & Bars and Business sections. Reliably re-reports openings, closings and awards - it has covered Taverna Sorrentina's opening, Canyon Club's Danville expansion and the Best of the East Bay lists. Michael Wittner is a Patch staff byline on Danville business coverage. Low-effort, high-frequency placement.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Social (Heather Ruiz)
local_media_and_influencers.note: HIGHEST-VALUE LOCAL INFLUENCER. Founded ~2018 by Heather Ruiz; roughly 11K Instagram followers and 10K+ website views/month. Tagline 'Be Seen. Support Local.' Covers restaurants, happy hours, events, holiday activities and business spotlights, and maintains a Danville business directory. Already publishes a Danville happy-hour guide that lists Danville Harvest (500 Hartz Ave, happy hour 7 days/week 3:30-5pm). Openly sells advertising: website placements, social media packages and featured write-ups. Phone (619) 944-5360. Note her happy-hour guide still lists the now-closed Cocina Hermanas, so an update pitch is a natural opening.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Your Town Monthly
local_media_and_influencers.note: Local lifestyle publication from S and J Advertising covering 12 East Bay and Solano communities including Danville, Pleasanton, Walnut Creek, Dublin and Livermore. Runs a recurring 'Taste of Your Town' restaurant spotlight - it profiled Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar (480 Hartz Ave) in August 2026, written by Assul Coss. Also runs an events calendar that carries Danville events (Hot Summer Sundays, Sip & Stroll, A Taste of Danville). Two of the four district restaurants are already in their orbit.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Beyond the Creek
local_media_and_influencers.note: Local news and lifestyle blog covering the greater Danville/Walnut Creek area with sections for restaurants, shopping, real estate and neighborhoods. Broke the Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar opening and covers the Danville Hotel Town Center tenant churn. Runs a newsletter and an advertiser program. Fast, informal - good for openings and 'new late menu' news.

local_media_and_influencers.name: ALIVE East Bay Magazine
local_media_and_influencers.note: ALIVE Media, 3200A Danville Blvd., Suite 204, Alamo, CA 94507 - physically in the district's own backyard. Regional lifestyle glossy.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Living
local_media_and_influencers.note: Best Version Media community magazine launched March 2016, mailed to Danville residents, built around neighbor-submitted stories and 'local, trusted businesses.' Also on Issuu. Pure resident-reach play rather than a food outlet.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Town of Danville official social
local_media_and_influencers.note: ~15K Instagram followers. The Town consolidated its Live Locally, Parks, Village Theatre and Art Gallery accounts into this single handle in May 2023; Public Information Officer Jenn Starnes. Posts arts, activities, projects and business news and uses #livelocallydanville. Social links at danville.ca.gov/stayconnected. Getting reshared here is free reach to the exact resident base.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Area Chamber of Commerce social
local_media_and_influencers.note: Social media promotion of members is an explicit membership benefit.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Farmers' Market
local_media_and_influencers.note: Weekly Saturday audience of downtown food shoppers - a natural cross-promotion partner.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Tim Cheung - Bay Area Foodies
local_media_and_influencers.note: 255,000 Instagram followers and 334,100 TikTok followers as reported by Diablo Magazine in its East Bay influencer roundup (published July 15, 2022 - counts are almost certainly higher now, verify before pitching). The largest food-specific account with genuine East Bay focus.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danielle Walker
local_media_and_influencers.note: 466,000 Instagram followers per Diablo Magazine (July 2022). A DANVILLE RESIDENT and best-selling gluten-free cookbook author. The highest-reach influencer who actually lives in town - a gluten-free-friendly late menu or a private tasting is an obvious hook.

local_media_and_influencers.name: East Bay Eats
local_media_and_influencers.note: ~4,518 followers; food and drink from the East Bay and beyond. Small but on-target, and #eastbayeats is one of the tags that actually co-occurs with #downtowndanville.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Bay Area Foodie Crew
local_media_and_influencers.note: ~23K followers, highlights spots across the Bay Area.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Bay Area Eats
local_media_and_influencers.note: ~5,390 followers; focused on eating, drinking and supporting small businesses.

local_media_and_influencers.name: Danville Harvest (district's own account, for benchmarking)
local_media_and_influencers.note: ~2,750 followers as shown in search results. Useful baseline: the district's combined owned audience is currently far smaller than Danville Social's 11K or the Town's 15K, so partner reach matters more than owned reach in year one.

hashtags_in_use: #LiveLocallyDanville - the Town of Danville's OFFICIAL campaign hashtag; residents, business owners and visitors are explicitly asked to use it (source: danville.ca.gov Live Locally campaign / Nextdoor announcement). Use this one on every post to get Town reshares.

#downtowndanville - the strongest genuinely local geo-tag; its top co-occurring tags are #danvilleca, #danvillecalifornia, #danville, #danvilleliving, #danvillerealestate, #trivalley, #eastbayeats, #trivalleylife, #bayareafoodie
#danvilleca - heavy real-estate and civic use as well as food; co-occurs with #sanramonca, #alamoca, #walnutcreekca, #danvilleliving, #blackhawkca
#danville - broad and diluted by Danville VA, PA, KY, IL and IN; never use alone

#danvilleeats - the clearest local FOOD tag; co-occurs with #trivalley, #sanramoneats, #pleasantoneats, #trivalleyeats, #danvilleliving, #danvilledining, #danvillefood, #eastbayeats, #danvillesocial, #yelpeastbay

#hartz - appears in the #downtowndanville cluster, a small but on-brand street tag
#trivalleyeats - the regional food tag, co-occurs with #danvilleca, #danvilleeats, #sanramoneats, #pleasantoneats

competitor_nightlife_zone.where: The NORTH end of downtown Danville - the 100-400 blocks of Hartz Avenue plus the Railroad Avenue / Prospect Avenue corridor, anchored by the Danville Hotel Town Center on Railroad Ave. That is roughly five to six blocks north of the district. For contrast, the four South of Hartz venues sit tightly clustered at the Hartz-and-Church corner: Incontro Ristorante 455 Hartz Ave (the historic Hartz House), Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar 480 Hartz Ave, Danville Harvest 500 Hartz Ave, and Rancho Cantina 501 Hartz Ave (the southeast corner of Hartz and Church, in the former Cocina Hermanas space). A secondary, separate late cluster sits southeast of downtown at the Danville Livery shopping center, 204 Sycamore Valley Road W, where Canyon Club Brewery runs a biergarten with firepits, heat lamps and a live-music stage.
example_venues: Elliott's Bar - 369 Hartz Ave. A dive bar in business over 100 years (briefly an ice cream parlor during Prohibition). Open 10:00 a.m. to 1:30 a.m. daily - by a wide margin the latest-closing venue in downtown Danville and the default destination after every other kitchen shuts.
Auburn Lounge & Wine Bar - 321 Hartz Ave. 1930s speakeasy feel. Mon-Wed 4 p.m.-midnight, Thu-Sun 2 p.m.-midnight.

Revel Kitchen & Bar - 331 Hartz Ave. Upscale-casual tavern from the owners of Esin, craft beer, cocktails and an eclectic wine list. Notably closes 9:00 p.m. Sun-Thu and 9:30 p.m. Fri-Sat, which is exactly the gap the district is targeting.
Danville Brewing Co. / DBC - 200 Railroad Ave, in the Danville Hotel Town Center. House beers plus guest drafts; a 2026 Diablo Magazine Best of the East Bay winner (Burger).

Crush'd Wine Bar Kitchen - downtown Danville. 24 wines on tap, craft cocktails, Apertivo Hour 3-6 p.m. daily ($12 cocktails, $9 small bites) and Live Music Thursdays. Markets itself explicitly 'from brunch to late night' - the closest direct competitor to the district's positioning.
11th Tiger - 171 Hartz Ave
Locanda Ravello - 172 E Prospect Ave
Le Petit Corner - 345 Railroad Ave
Primo's Pizzeria & Pub - downtown; happy hour daily 3-6 p.m.
The Growler - happy hour Tuesdays 4-9 p.m., Wed-Fri 3-6 p.m.

Canyon Club Brewery - Danville Livery, 204 Sycamore Valley Rd W (separate cluster southeast of downtown). Taproom, restaurant and pilot brewery with a patio biergarten, firepits and a live-music stage.
competitor_nightlife_zone.description: Danville's noisier, younger, later-running drinking scene is concentrated at the top of Hartz Avenue and around the Danville Hotel Town Center on Railroad Ave, not at the Church Street end. The mix there is a century-old dive (Elliott's, open to 1:30 a.m.), a speakeasy-styled wine lounge (Auburn), a brewery taproom (Danville Brewing) and a self-described 'brunch to late night' wine bar (Crush'd) - venues built around drinking, standing and staying, with a beer-and-cocktail price point. The Danville Livery biergarten pulls a similar crowd off-downtown. Three things make South of Hartz's upscale-alternative positioning defensible. First, geography: the four district restaurants form a genuinely contiguous four-corner block at Hartz and Church, five-plus blocks from that cluster - close enough to be downtown, far enough to read as its own place. Second, the 8-10 p.m. gap is real and documented, not assumed: even the good sit-down rooms at the north end close at 9-9:30 p.m., and a Tri-Valley Foodist piece quoted a local observing that restaurants in Danville get all the attention, i.e. the town is restaurant-centric rather than bar-centric. Third, the district's own mix is already differentiated - a historic-house Italian room, a tiki bar, a farm-to-table kitchen and a wood-fired Mexican cantina - which supports a dinner-here, nightcap-and-dessert-there cross-visit story that a row of bars cannot tell. The realistic competitive risk is Crush'd, which already claims the late-night language, and Elliott's, which owns the after-9:30 default by simple fact of being open.

data.notes: WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM (do not treat these as established): (1) FOLLOWER COUNTS. Instagram blocks automated reads, so every follower number here comes from a search-result snippet or a cited article, not from the profile itself. The @bayarea.foodies (255K IG / 334.1K TikTok) and @daniellewalker (466K) figures come from a Diablo Magazine roundup published July 15, 2022 and are certainly stale. @danvillesocial ~11K, @danvillecagov ~15K, @danvilleharvest ~2,750 and @eastbayeats ~4,518 come from search snippets quoting the live profiles. Re-verify manually before building a media plan around any of them. (2) DANVILLE FALLFEST STATUS. Fallfest is absent from the Town's 2026 community events list and danvillefallfest.com returned no content. It may be discontinued or folded into Fall Hallo-Wine. Its historic street closures included Church Street between Railroad and Hartz - the district's own corner - so its status matters. Confirm with the chamber. (3) FALL HALLO-WINE DETAILS. I have only the Town's one-line listing (Oct 28, 2026, chamber, downtown). No dedicated event page exists yet; earlier editions ran as Flavors of Fall, Oktoberfest and Fall Rock & Stroll. (4) 2027 TASTE TRI-VALLEY DATES are unannounced; the page says to watch it. (5) CHAMBER MEMBERSHIP PRICING is not published anywhere public - the Why Join page references a Membership Toolkit but shows no tiers or dollar figures. Ask Amy Millington directly. (6) NO LOCAL PODCAST FOUND. There is no Danville CA or Tri-Valley food/nightlife podcast that I could verify. The 'Danville Podcast' on Apple Podcasts is a high-school class production from a different Danville. Treat a podcast as a gap to create rather than a channel to pitch. (7) DISCOVER DANVILLE ASSOCIATION appears defunct (last IRS filing FY2016, absent from the current IRS exempt list). 'Discover Danville' today means the Town's walking-tour web app. Also note discoverdanvilleca.com is an unrelated spam travel blog and discoverdanville.com is Danville VIRGINIA - a large share of web results for 'Danville' are Virginia, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Illinois or Indiana, so verify the state on anything not sourced here. (8) DANVILLE MERCHANTS' ASSOCIATION has no findable website or contact; it is known only from the Town's attribution of the Hot Summer Sundays Car Show. (9) HASHTAG DATA comes from best-hashtags.com co-occurrence data (a real aggregation of Instagram usage), not from Instagram directly; treat relative popularity as indicative rather than exact. (10) HOURS quoted for competitor venues come from Yelp/OpenTable listings surfaced in search and change frequently - verify before publishing any comparison. THREE FINDINGS WORTH ACTING ON FIRST: (a) The brand names are CLEAN. best-hashtags.com returns 'not found' for #danvilleafterdark, #southofhartz AND #danvillenightlife - none of the three is currently in use, so the district can own all of them outright. (b) Danville Harvest is already credited by the Town as the organizer of a downtown Neighborhood Street Party (June 20, 2026), which means one of the four partners has already walked the Town's approval path for a street-level event. (c) The Town's Economic Development Division explicitly funds 'collaborative community events,' and none of the four restaurants won a 2026 Diablo Best of the East Bay award - so there is both money and an uncontested award category available. Also flag for the site build: the Planning Commission was reviewing PERMANENT outdoor-dining rules on Sept 8, 2026 (current temporary rules expire Jan 2, 2027), and the draft explicitly PROHIBITS parklets on Hartz Avenue while capping downtown parklets at 12 spaces - directly relevant to any patio-based late-night concept.
